extracted.intended_audience: general readers / students of personal hygiene and public health (early 20th century)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical hygiene and health recommendations for individuals covering diet, exercise, clothing, bathing, ventilation, teeth/eyes, sleep, and avoidance of stimulants and drugs. Advice is aimed at preserving vitality and preventing disease through daily habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention and enjoyment at meals
rubrics_metrics.description: The thought or anticipation of pleasant food stimulates production of digestive juices; enjoyment of food is important to digestion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eating without interest or attention is likely to produce subsequent indigestion; the attitude toward a meal (leisurely, pleasurable) affects digestion as much as the food itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid violent exercise after meals
rubrics_metrics.description: Violent exercise after eating is undesirable because it diverts vitality from stomach and intestines to other muscles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vigorous exercise after heavy meals is condemned; moderate exercise after ordinary meals is not objectionable. Mental exercise after an ordinary meal is not shown to be harmful unless the meal was excessive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily water consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: The body requires a constant replenishing of liquids; the ordinary person ought to consume at least two quarts of water a day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many liver, kidney, and other difficulties would be avoided by this intake. Drinking water at meals is not particularly harmful except that continual swallowing may encourage swallowing without chewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of condiments and salt
rubrics_metrics.description: Condiments and drinks (salt, pepper, vinegar, spices) have negligible nutritive value but play an important role in suggesting pleasure and stimulating digestive juices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salt is physiologically craved and must be provided in some quantity; sameness of food reduces appetite and hence digestive stimulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautions about tea and coffee
rubrics_metrics.description: Coffee and tea are consumed for pleasure but have a stimulating effect; excessive use can deplete nerves and muscular tissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated use to stave off tiredness comes at the expense of bodily tissues; tea boiled long develops tannin (astringent, injurious to stomach). Tea without milk is said to be safer because boiling is less likely when bitter taste is apparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alcohol is harmful
rubrics_metrics.description: Alcohol, in any form (spirits, wines, beer, cider), adversely affects memory, will, intellect, and muscular tissue and reduces capacity for activity and endurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No small amount will add to living tissue; it merely stimulates and exhausts the nervous/muscular systems. It is worse than useless as protection against cold; the feeling of warmth is deceptive and dangerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tobacco cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tobacco's essential poison (nicotine) affects the heart and nerve cells; habitual use commonly leads to reduced respiratory capacity and other harms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Young people, especially boys training athletically, should not smoke; children should not smoke because it interferes with full development of heart and nervous system. Effects vary by individual constitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding drug habits and patent medicines
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of narcotic drugs (morphine, opium, cocaine) leads to addiction and ruin; patent medicines are often swindles and may contain dangerous substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent medicines should be avoided unless they carry their formula on the label and are prescribed by a reputable physician. Consumptive diseases and cancer are not cured by such drugs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular, varied exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: For perfect health each part of the body should receive exercise; exercise promotes lung tissue, oxygenation, waste removal, appetite, digestion, and intestinal absorptive power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise should affect all muscles, not be confined to one set (irregular/partial exercise can lead later to waste). Deep breathing and increased lung action during exercise are important benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clothing to regulate evaporation and protect
rubrics_metrics.description: Clothing's object is to protect against weather (cold, wet, heat) and injury, and to preserve and make uniform evaporation from the body so as to maintain temperature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loose, porous garments that hold air are better insulators than tightly woven ones; multiple light layers outperform one heavy layer of equal weight. Amount and kind of clothing should depend on individual vitality and occupation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Woolen underwear recommendations and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Wool is an effective non-conductor and often recommended for undergarments because it retains heat and checks chill from perspiration evaporation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wool can irritate sensitive skin; partially woolen undergarments may be a compromise. Heavy woolen clothing is unnecessary indoors if rooms are well heated; older or sedentary persons may need more warmth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outer garments should be windproof and air-retaining
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficient outer garments must have an impervious surface so winds cannot penetrate and a loose open weave to hold air for warmth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and material should prevent wind penetration while trapping insulating air.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rubber boots for foot health
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubber boots do not allow perspiration to evaporate and hold the foot moist, which is detrimental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer rubber-cloth overshoes, arctics, or felt overshoes; cloth shoes can relieve chilblains fostered by rubber boots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ventilate bedrooms; prefer sleeping with window open
rubrics_metrics.description: Breathing repeatedly one's expired air is unhealthy; bedroom ventilation is important to eliminate organic impurities and supply oxygen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sleeping with a window open (with enough bed clothing) is encouraged; a cheesecloth screen prevents draft yet allows ventilation. Airtight rooms with double windows and sealed cracks make ventilation necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bedding choices: many light blankets over one heavy
rubrics_metrics.description: Two lightly woven blankets are preferable to one heavy blanket; wool bedding is better than cotton and quilts should be loose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper bedclothing allows enjoying night air without danger if adequate insulation is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent bathing and cleanliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Bathing removes oily deposits and scurf on skin that clog glands and may putrefy; cleanliness discourages infection and disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinary bath temperature should be between 90 and 100 degrees Fahrenheit with enough soap. Frequency depends on constitution, season, work, and household conveniences. Bath facilities in homes greatly improve public health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cold baths only with demonstrated tonic benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Cold baths can have a tonic effect if followed by a good reaction, but they are not universally beneficial and may cause later depression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cold baths for tonic effect should be used only when the individual is assured of lasting benefits; baths for cleanliness are universally desirable; tonic baths may be omitted if not pleasurable or beneficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent hand washing to reduce contagion
rubrics_metrics.description: Washing hands often is highly effective in reducing the ravages of contagious diseases because hands most frequently transmit germs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guests should accept an invitation to wash before dinner as an act of courtesy and infection control; doctors wash hands often even without apparent exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer nose breathing; avoid mouth breathing
rubrics_metrics.description: Breathing through the nose is intended to filter and condition air; mouth breathing lacks filtering and tends to induce tonsil inflammation and adenoids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mouth breathing can cause characteristic facial expression, retard mental and moral development in children, produce earache, deafness, and inflamed eyes. Enlarged tonsils/adenoids that obstruct nostrils should be removed (simple operation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eye care and screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Many incidental troubles (headache, sleeplessness) and school problems (backwardness, truancy) are due to weak or strained eyes; defective vision is common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use eye-testing and consult an oculist rather than buying spectacles from jewelers or peddlers; an oculist can measure each eye and fit correct lenses. In rural areas outdoor life may mask defects but professional care is still advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dental care: chew well, brush, and visit dentist
rubrics_metrics.description: Teeth are essential to proper mastication; decayed or malpositioned teeth hinder mastication and harbor germs that can infect many organs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage toothbrush use from age four and habitually twice a day; periodic dental examination at least once a year by a qualified dentist is recommended. Persistent cleaning after eating (as in Armenian children) reduces dental disease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right amount of sleep
rubrics_metrics.description: Sleep restores tired muscles and jaded nerves and is necessary for rebuilding tissue; lack of sleep brings nervous disaster while too much sleep is shirking duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brain work increases sleep need more than purely muscular work; sleep deprivation causes cognitive and motor dysfunction. Oversleeping reduces active life and is detrimental to personal development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disease is multifactorial and relative to individual normal
rubrics_metrics.description: Disease is an abnormal condition but what is abnormal varies by individual; disease is usually the result of multiple linked causes, not a single cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding disease requires considering individual normality and multiple contributing circumstances rather than seeking one special cause.
